subject: Food Science
title: Salt and Sugar Preservation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Salt and Sugar Preservation.

hook.text: Salt cod fed European empires. Sugar preserved fruit for centuries. The oldest preservatives are in your kitchen.

buildup.text: Salt and sugar preserve food by binding water molecules, leaving too little available moisture for bacteria.

discovery.text: Water activity below 0.85 stops most bacterial growth. Salt and sugar lower water activity efficiently.

twist.text: Modern health concerns about salt and sugar have made the oldest preservatives controversial too.

climax.text: Reduced-sodium products need replacement preservatives. Removing salt creates new technical challenges.

punchline.text: The simplest preservatives work best. But now we worry about them too.

quiz.question: How do salt and sugar preserve food?
options: They bind water molecules, reducing available moisture for microbial growth
